title: Week 27 Mastery Quiz · Global Political Economy, Trade, and Debt

questions.question: Which definition best matches “global value chain”?
options: Cross-border organization of production stages for a good or service.
The capacity to shape behavior, choices, rules, opportunities, or outcomes.
Recognition for mastery above the minimum course threshold.
A record explaining changes made in response to evidence and feedback.
questions.explanation: Global value chain means cross-border organization of production stages for a good or service.

questions.question: Which definition best matches “foreign direct investment”?
options: A systematic review of required work, evidence, records, and corrections.
Investment providing lasting control or influence in an enterprise abroad.
Inventing evidence, data, sources, quotations, or results.
A condition or benefit understood to serve the community as a whole.
questions.explanation: Foreign direct investment means investment providing lasting control or influence in an enterprise abroad.

questions.question: Which definition best matches “sovereign debt”?
options: Money owed by a national government.
A standard for fair institutions, rights, duties, procedures, and distributions.
Protection that makes a constitutional rule harder to change than ordinary law.
Using different sources or methods to examine the same question.
questions.explanation: Sovereign debt means money owed by a national government.

questions.question: Which definition best matches “balance of payments”?
options: A record of transactions between residents of a country and the rest of the world.
A state in which ultimate constitutional authority rests with the central government.
Freedom from unjust restraint and the capacity to make meaningful choices.
A legal tradition centered on comprehensive codes and enacted law.
questions.explanation: Balance of payments means a record of transactions between residents of a country and the rest of the world.

questions.question: Which definition best matches “sanction”?
options: A subset studied to estimate characteristics of a larger population.
The capacity of courts to decide cases without improper political control.
The foundational rules organizing government, authority, rights, and amendment.
A restriction intended to influence another actor’s behavior.
questions.explanation: Sanction means a restriction intended to influence another actor’s behavior.

questions.question: Which definition best matches “debt sustainability”?
options: The legal right to vote.
A government’s capacity to meet debt obligations without unacceptable adjustment or default.
False or manipulated information spread deliberately.
The ability of public institutions to implement decisions and provide core functions.
questions.explanation: Debt sustainability means a government’s capacity to meet debt obligations without unacceptable adjustment or default.

questions.question: Which statement is most consistent with the Week 27 analysis?
options: The most confident source should be accepted without examining authority or method.
A single vivid example proves a universal conclusion without qualification.
Trade can create aggregate gains while imposing concentrated adjustment costs.
Political labels have exactly the same meaning in every country and period.
questions.explanation: Trade can create aggregate gains while imposing concentrated adjustment costs.

questions.question: Which statement is most consistent with the Week 27 analysis?
options: Financial integration transmits capital and crises.
The most confident source should be accepted without examining authority or method.
Political labels have exactly the same meaning in every country and period.
A single vivid example proves a universal conclusion without qualification.
questions.explanation: Financial integration transmits capital and crises.

questions.question: Which research practice is most appropriate for Global Political Economy, Trade, and Debt?
options: Trace claims to WTO records, trade data, sovereign-debt cases, supply-chain maps, and labor evidence, evaluate authority and context, corroborate material facts, and state limitations.
Use the first search result and treat its summary as conclusive.
Choose only evidence that supports the preferred conclusion.
Replace documentary evidence with political identity or intuition.
questions.explanation: Trace claims to WTO records, trade data, sovereign-debt cases, supply-chain maps, and labor evidence, evaluate authority and context, corroborate material facts, and state limitations.

questions.question: Which response most clearly demonstrates senior-level mastery?
options: List facts without connecting them to a claim.
Use a slogan as the conclusion and omit uncertainties.
Define the terms, compare evidence, explain reasoning, address a serious alternative, and name a revision condition.
Treat legal, causal, and moral claims as interchangeable.
questions.explanation: Define the terms, compare evidence, explain reasoning, address a serious alternative, and name a revision condition.

shortResponse: Who gains, who loses, and who decides in systems of global trade, finance, investment, taxation, and debt?
rubric: 10 points: precise claim (2), accurate concepts (2), two specific pieces of evidence (2), reasoning (2), counterargument or limitation (1), revision condition (1).
